    - You're standing on the counterweight's shadow. Means nothing. Just thought you'd want to know where you are.
    - *Player*. That adder-skin cord's the best line I've had on this lift. Not one fray. I check it every morning anyway.
    - *Player*. Leland says the winch down the old well runs sweeter than his knees. I'll take that. Two lifts in this city now, sort of. One just happens to go down.
    - What?
        - *Choice:* How does the lift work?

    - Ropes, a hand-winch, a platform and a counterweight of old fortress stones, all bolted to the old granary at the end of the Row. Built it three years ago. I was nineteen. Everyone said it wouldn't hold.
    - My mother hauled crates up the rooftop stairs for twenty years till her back gave out. Hedda. Porters work the winch now and nobody's back gives out. That's why it's there. Not to sparkle.
    - Near the Old Barracks, over the public stair. Theatre folk haul scenery up to the roofs every Walkout Day by hand. But it's a public stair, so the Table has to agree. I've stood up twice. Bastian's covered bridge talked over me both times. Loud man. Nice man. Loud.
    - Margo builds things that go bang and might work. I build things that work and don't go bang. We argue every day. She's wrong about springs.
    - Last winter a crate of Tinsel's glass jammed halfway up and Margo climbed the ropes with a spanner in her teeth. I rehung her door the last time she blew it off. That's how it goes. Don't tell her I said any of that.
